title: Shiva's household, exactly as told in live run 11

order_in.note: we eat out on Sunday lunch

told.family: It's me Shiva, my wife Ankita, our son Agastya who is 8, our daughter Meera who is 4, and my mother Lakshmi, she's 65.
told.cook: We have a cook, she comes Monday to Saturday, 7 to 9 in the morning and 6 to 7:30 in the evening.
told.cookLimits: She doesn't bake, we have no oven. Phulkas she makes but not more than twice a week, it takes her too long.
told.cookTime: Mornings are tight: at most 2 dishes in the morning and breakfast must be done in under 20 minutes.
told.newRecipes: She can try one new dish a week, but never on a weekday dinner, evenings are too rushed.
told.cookingDays: Sunday the cook is off. Sunday breakfast my wife and I cook, something South Indian. Sunday lunch we eat out. Sunday dinner has to be something under 15 minutes.
told.kidsBreakfast: Meera only eats plain idli, plain dosa or banana sheera for breakfast, nothing else. Agastya eats what we eat.
told.kidsLunch: Agastya takes a tiffin to school Monday to Friday: it must be dry, nut-free (school rule), and never the same thing twice in a week. Meera eats lunch at home and it has to be soft.
told.kidsDinner: Agastya won't eat anything if he sees something green in it. Meera can't have anything spicy: keep her portion aside before the chilli goes in.
told.adultsLunch: I need protein at every lunch and dinner — dal, paneer, chana, anything.
told.adultsDinner: Same, protein for me at dinner.
told.diet: Strictly vegetarian, no eggs. No mushrooms. Nobody eats bitter gourd or brinjal. And Ankita has a peanut allergy, so no peanuts and no groundnut oil anywhere in the house.
told.elders: My mother is diabetic: no white rice for her, give her millets instead, and no sugar.
told.rules: Tuesday the whole family eats Jain: no onion, no garlic, no potato, no root vegetables. Thursday my mother fasts: she eats only sabudana khichdi or fruits that day.
told.orderIn: Sunday lunch we eat out. Nothing else is ordered.
